newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch swine fever toll tops 200, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Dutch swine fever toll tops 200, seen rising.

text.p: The number of farms hit by classical swine fever in the Netherlands totalled more than 200 on Tuesday and the Dutch Agriculture Minister forecast the toll rising further before the authorities could bring the outbreak under control.
"There will be more cases, that is certain. Probably, it will grow to 300," Jozias van Aartsen told reporters during an informal meeting of European Union Farm Ministers.
All cases are concentrated in the south of the country, where a ban on the transport of all livestock has been in force soon after the contagious disease was detected early this year.
"Thanks to the measures we have taken, the disease has been contained," Van Aartsen added.
But he conceded that the cost has been enormous. Somewhere near two million pigs have now been killed at a total cost of one billion guilders. The EU has footed much of the bill.

"This is an urgent and dramatic problem and the European Union has helped in a great way," he said. He added he had used the meeting, hosted by the Dutch who hold the EU Presidency, to liaise with his Spanish counterpart Loyola de Palacio.
Spain has also been hit by an outbreak of the disease but Van Aartsen said this had now been brought under control there.
The Dutch government is now pinning its hopes on a new kind of vaccine, developed by Dutch scientists, which is says will allow the easier segregation of infected animals.

It hopes to have this so-called "marker vaccine" in use by the beginning of next year but such a move would require a change in EU policy, which currently does not permit the vaccination of animals against infectious diseases.
"We are talking to Spain, Denmark and Germany about this and we hope to have it in the market by early next year," he said.
